item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-3c3762c63f8d8ebc","start_unit":1,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The 2023 IMSS-BIENESTAR operating rules formally established a federal health program for people without social security, linking free health services, medicines and supplies to the MAS-BIENESTAR model and requiring gender equity, an intercultural approach and human-rights compliance. The rules were mandatory for 2023 but subject to annual congressional budget availability.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly applicable to 2023; the rules entered into force on 1 January 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The program was part of the federal government’s health policy under López Obrador, but the instrument was issued by IMSS Director General Zoé Robledo.","limitations":["This establishes formal design and authority, not actual service quality or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3c3762c63f8d8ebc","start_unit":22,"end_unit":30,"fact_summary":"IMSS-BIENESTAR defined prevention, epidemiological surveillance, ambulatory and hospital care, medicines, rehabilitation, community participation and citizen oversight for people without social security. It reported 4,075 hospitals and health units nationally, with itinerant services for dispersed populations, and planned federalization to expand free universal coverage. Beneficiary registration and coverage were tied to a population registry that could include migrants receiving services.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The operating rules applied during 2023, although the facility count was based primarily on a September 2022 catalogue.","ruler_attribution":"The arrangements implemented the federal administration’s health and federalization agenda.","limitations":["The document describes planned or authorized coverage and does not establish that all listed services were delivered effectively."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3c3762c63f8d8ebc","start_unit":38,"end_unit":45,"fact_summary":"The program required preventive and integrated care, patient safety, evidence-based practice, dignity, non-discrimination, continuous-improvement plans, staff training, patient-rights protections and complaint systems. Beneficiaries were entitled to free, equal and confidential care, informed consent, second opinions, emergency attention and responses to complaints through institutional bodies and citizen representatives.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.8","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 operating framework.","ruler_attribution":"These were federal program requirements adopted during López Obrador’s administration.","limitations":["The rules do not demonstrate compliance in practice or remedy of violations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3c3762c63f8d8ebc","start_unit":42,"end_unit":49,"fact_summary":"IMSS-BIENESTAR established multidisciplinary supervision, advisory visits, written commitments, performance and quality reviews, corrective measures, internal and external evaluations, public reporting of external evaluations, and authority for the program unit to administer resources, training, procurement, infrastructure and improvement actions.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","6B.4","6B.5","6B.9","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The mechanisms were prescribed for the 2023 fiscal year.","ruler_attribution":"The rules placed implementation and oversight within federal administrative structures of the López Obrador government.","limitations":["These are formal controls; the source does not report their effectiveness or independence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3c3762c63f8d8ebc","start_unit":60,"end_unit":68,"fact_summary":"The program linked budgeting to national plans and results indicators, assigned funds by coverage and activity, required separate and detailed accounting, returned unspent funds to the Treasury, subjected expenditures to federal audits, and required internal follow-up on audit recommendations. Internal monitoring used a dashboard and external evaluations by recognized specialists whose results were to be public.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","6B.5","8B.3","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The rules governed fiscal year 2023, while some budget planning occurred before the year began.","ruler_attribution":"These controls were established through the federal program administered by IMSS.","limitations":["No actual audit findings, spending outcomes or corrective records are supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3c3762c63f8d8ebc","start_unit":68,"end_unit":76,"fact_summary":"The program specified 19 performance indicators covering infant, maternal and neonatal mortality, diabetes, vaccination, hypertension, medicine supply, complaints, detection and follow-up, prenatal care, sanitation and referrals. It required reporting through the federal performance system, transparency-law compliance, social auditing and investigation and notification of complaints.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.8","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Indicators and accountability procedures were specified for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The indicators and transparency mechanisms were part of the federal administration’s program design.","limitations":["The source does not provide 2023 indicator results or evidence that complaints were resolved."]},{"source_id":"SRC-42b417feb578efb9","start_unit":1,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International reported that Mexico supported recommendations on investigating and sanctioning security-force abuses, protecting journalists, strengthening the National Human Rights Commission and repealing arraigo, but assessed major implementation failures: impunity persisted, journalist investigations were inadequate, arraigo remained in force, and the NHRC’s autonomy had not been strengthened.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.10","4B.4","4B.6","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was published in July 2023 and reviewed the situation relevant to the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern the Mexican government under López Obrador, while recommendations and prior commitments involved the state institutionally.","limitations":["Amnesty is an external rights-monitoring organization and some assessments summarize developments predating 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-42b417feb578efb9","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The president publicly attacked the Supreme Court when it blocked placing the National Guard under military control and accused Indigenous and environmental defenders criticizing the Maya Train of being “false environmentalists.” Amnesty also reported stigmatization of journalists, NGOs and protesters by high authorities, alongside excessive force, arbitrary arrests, sexual violence and criminalization of protest with widespread impunity.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.4","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report documents conduct and institutional conditions relevant to 2023, including the Supreme Court’s April 2023 ruling.","ruler_attribution":"The public statements and political attacks were attributed directly to López Obrador; other abuses involved state and local authorities.","limitations":["The source does not establish that every protest-related abuse was personally directed by the president."]},{"source_id":"SRC-42b417feb578efb9","start_unit":13,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"Official data cited by Amnesty recorded at least 20,292 women killed between 2018 and May 2023, with 5,065 investigated as alleged feminicides. Despite 25 gender-violence alerts in 22 states, Amnesty reported unabated impunity, lost evidence, inadequate investigations, insufficient gender perspective and threats or revictimization of victims’ families.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.3","6B.5","7B.2","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly includes data through May 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The outcomes concern the Mexican state during López Obrador’s presidency; the failures were often located in prosecutors’ offices and other authorities.","limitations":["The document reports national outcomes and institutional failures but does not prove personal presidential knowledge of each case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-42b417feb578efb9","start_unit":24,"end_unit":29,"fact_summary":"Public security remained heavily militarized: the National Guard was strongly influenced by the Armed Forces, military participation in public security was extended toward 2028, and the Supreme Court struck down the 2022 transfer of Guard control to SEDENA in April 2023. Human-rights complaints against the Guard, SEDENA and SEMAR included arbitrary detention, torture, enforced disappearance and other abuses; Amnesty linked military participation to reduced transparency and accountability.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","8B.2","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source includes the April 2023 Supreme Court decision and reports complaint totals through 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Amnesty states that militarization was defended and promoted by López Obrador and furthered by Congress.","limitations":["Complaint totals precede 2023 and do not by themselves establish the president’s direct responsibility for each alleged violation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-42b417feb578efb9","start_unit":8,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"Mexico ratified the Kampala amendments to the Rome Statute in 2021 and formally recognized the UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances’ competence to receive individual complaints in 2020. These were positive accountability steps, but the use-of-force law remained inconsistent with international standards, arraigo remained unrepealed despite Inter-American Court orders, and NHRC autonomy remained incomplete.","question_ids":["2B.9","3B.4","3B.5","3B.10","4B.4","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The acts occurred before 2023 but their implementation status was assessed in the 2023 submission.","ruler_attribution":"These were commitments and institutional actions of the Mexican government under López Obrador.","limitations":["The source does not show whether the positive commitments produced measurable 2023 remedies."]},{"source_id":"SRC-71a459cd1d3200fc","start_unit":2,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"CIDOB describes López Obrador as president from 2018 to 2024 and identifies his governing program as centered on austerity, social programs, reducing poverty and violence, energy and food self-sufficiency, anti-corruption, a gradual military withdrawal from internal security, and cooperation with the United States. The platform combined social spending with macroeconomic stability, budget discipline and rejection of privatization in strategic sectors.","question_ids":["2B.10","3B.10","4B.10","5B.1","5B.3","6B.1","6B.3","8B.1"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"This is a political biography updated in 2018 and therefore provides programmatic baseline rather than direct 2023 evidence.","ruler_attribution":"The program and commitments are attributed to López Obrador and MORENA.","limitations":["The source was not updated to assess 2023 implementation or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-71a459cd1d3200fc","start_unit":19,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"López Obrador’s 2018 program called for legal reform, anti-corruption, poverty reduction, peace, austerity, gender equity, sustainable development and reconstruction. It proposed a civilian-command National Guard to replace the Army in internal security, while his election victory gave the governing coalition majorities in both federal chambers and broad subnational representation.","question_ids":["3B.6","4B.1","4B.2","5B.1","6B.1","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The program and electoral mandate predate 2023 and are relevant as frozen goals and authority baseline.","ruler_attribution":"The program was López Obrador’s and the majorities belonged to his coalition.","limitations":["The source does not establish that the civilian-command security goal was achieved."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cb7adb2d19e644c1","start_unit":5,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"CSIS assessed López Obrador’s policies as mixed or counterproductive in several areas: expansion of military influence despite demilitarization rhetoric, centralization of power, weakening of independent checks, weak nearshoring strategy and deteriorating security. It also credited his personal austerity, anti-corruption rhetoric, avoidance of a major pandemic fiscal crisis and successful negotiation of the USMCA.","question_ids":["2B.10","3B.10","4B.4","4B.10","5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.10","7B.1","7B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Published July 2023 and directly evaluates the administration before the 2024 transition.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment concerns López Obrador’s presidency and policies.","limitations":["The report is an analytical assessment rather than an official audit; some claims rely on cited secondary sources."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cb7adb2d19e644c1","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"López Obrador halted new foreign oil contracts, audited more than 100 previous awards for corruption and committed billions to the Dos Bocas refinery, but the refinery was reported substantially over budget. His proposed electricity reform would have strengthened state control and subordinated autonomous regulators; Congress failed to approve it, limiting his ability to enact the full agenda. Lithium nationalization and hostility to foreign energy investment raised concerns about investor confidence and clean-energy transition.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","7B.9","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The assessment covers policies and legislative outcomes through 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The decisions and legislative initiative were attributed to López Obrador’s administration.","limitations":["The report includes forecasts and estimates as well as completed policy actions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cb7adb2d19e644c1","start_unit":12,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"The administration concentrated development efforts in southern Mexico through Sembrando Vida, Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro, Dos Bocas, the Maya Train and the Isthmus corridor. CSIS reported substantial beneficiary reach and possible economic benefits, but also cited possible deforestation, alleged political patronage and arbitrary scholarship allocation, cost overruns, environmental risks and exclusion of some of the poorest municipalities.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.10","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report was published in 2023 and evaluates projects and programs active during the period.","ruler_attribution":"The initiatives were identified as López Obrador administration priorities.","limitations":["Several negative findings are based on cited external investigations and projected outcomes rather than final 2023 evaluations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cb7adb2d19e644c1","start_unit":14,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"Tax collection and fiscal management improved in some respects: the tax-to-GDP ratio rose 1.6 percentage points between 2019 and 2020, Mexico maintained manageable debt and a balanced budget in 2022, and restrained pandemic spending avoided a large primary deficit. Conversely, austerity coincided with business losses and budget cuts to agencies viewed as politically hostile, while military control over infrastructure and economic projects expanded.","question_ids":["4B.4","5B.1","5B.3","5B.5","5B.6","5B.10","7B.9","8B.3","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report was published in July 2023; fiscal indicators include 2019-2022 data and the institutional trend continued into 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The fiscal and administrative choices were attributed to López Obrador’s government.","limitations":["The source does not isolate the effects of external pandemic conditions from government policy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cb7adb2d19e644c1","start_unit":17,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"CSIS reported record-level violence during López Obrador’s term: approximately 34,000 homicides in 2021, 2022 as the most violent year recorded by the national system, political assassinations in the 2021 midterms, and criminal organizations controlling up to 40 percent of Mexican territory. The report judged the “hugs, not bullets” approach ineffective and associated it with reduced security spending, weakened U.S. cooperation and expanding organized crime.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.8","2B.10","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published in 2023 and evaluates outcomes during the presidency through 2022 and early 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The security strategy and policy choices were attributed to López Obrador.","limitations":["Security outcomes are affected by longstanding criminal fragmentation and external factors; the report presents an analytical causal assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cb7adb2d19e644c1","start_unit":22,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"The report linked militarization and cartel expansion to severe human-rights risks, journalist killings, femicides and impunity. It stated that López Obrador increased army and marine budgets, made the National Guard a de facto auxiliary military force, extended military street patrols to 2028, and continued deployments despite allegations of civilian killings, cover-ups and persistent low case-resolution rates.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.7","3B.8","3B.10","4B.4","8B.2","8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report’s assessment was current to July 2023, though several cited incidents predate 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Military budgets, deployments and security reforms were attributed to López Obrador’s administration.","limitations":["The report aggregates incidents and trends and does not establish personal involvement in each abuse."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cb7adb2d19e644c1","start_unit":26,"end_unit":28,"fact_summary":"CSIS reported budget cuts and political pressure affecting the INE, INAI, COFECE and CNDH; alleged attacks on NGOs, defenders, media and anti-corruption initiatives; and an electoral Plan B that reduced the electoral arbiter’s powers and was fast-tracked. The Supreme Court later invalidated important parts of Plan B, suspended other provisions and preserved institutional checks, while the INE conducted successful local elections in June 2023.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.8","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly relevant to 2023, including the Senate’s February approval and court decisions through June 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The reforms, budget proposals and attacks were attributed to López Obrador; the constraints came from Congress, courts and civil society.","limitations":["The report uses strong analytical language and incorporates cited commentary from other observers."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cb7adb2d19e644c1","start_unit":29,"end_unit":34,"fact_summary":"Despite tensions, Mexico maintained substantial U.S. economic integration and participated in 2023 North American cooperation on supply chains and semiconductors. At the same time, disputes over energy and genetically modified corn, limits on DEA cooperation, strained security relations and ideological disagreements created uncertainty for trade, investment and counternarcotics cooperation.","question_ids":["1B.4","2B.5","2B.7","2B.10","5B.4","5B.10","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report includes the 2023 North American Leaders’ Summit and ongoing 2023 disputes.","ruler_attribution":"Foreign-policy and cooperation choices were attributed to López Obrador’s government, while bilateral outcomes reflected both governments.","limitations":["The source focuses on outlook and policy implications rather than a complete record of executed diplomatic decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b23538414c59c878","start_unit":4,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Banco de México’s deputy governor described Mexico’s post-pandemic recovery as slow but supported by solid macroeconomic fundamentals, conservative pandemic fiscal policy, manageable current-account levels and a relatively low primary balance. The presentation also identified high inflation, incomplete recovery, weak investment and uncertainty from global tightening and the Ukraine conflict.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The presentation concerns February 2022 conditions and is contextual rather than direct 2023 evidence.","ruler_attribution":"It evaluates Mexico’s macroeconomic position during López Obrador’s administration but expressly states that the views are the author’s and not necessarily Banco de México’s institutional position.","limitations":["The source predates 2023 and does not attribute monetary policy decisions directly to the president."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b23538414c59c878","start_unit":11,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"The presentation found that by late 2021 total employment had recovered its pre-pandemic level, while formal employment remained below its long-run trend; private consumption and investment gaps persisted, and credit to firms lagged trend. Public investment had begun to recover after a long decline but remained below historical maximum levels.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence describes 2021 conditions and is a baseline for assessing the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The indicators concern national outcomes during López Obrador’s administration, without proving presidential causation.","limitations":["The document does not provide 2023 outcomes or a policy attribution analysis."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c27c10e952de9faf","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL reported that the administration’s 16 priority social programs had a 2022 original budget of 506.543 billion pesos, 71% above 2019 in real terms. In 2021 they reached 27 million people, or 64% of their identified target population, while 56% of programs achieved adequate or outstanding effective target compliance.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.10","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The report was published in October 2022 and covers results through 2021, providing pre-2023 evidence.","ruler_attribution":"The programs were established and funded under the López Obrador administration.","limitations":["The report does not measure 2022 or 2023 outcomes and coverage calculations depend on available administrative data."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c27c10e952de9faf","start_unit":20,"end_unit":26,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL found major improvement in the design of priority-program results matrices: programs with adequate or outstanding overall design rose from 26% in 2020 to 50% in 2022. However, six programs lacked a consolidated results orientation, 31% lacked suitable outcome indicators, and health and university programs remained especially weak. The health program’s objective shifted from delivering effective and equitable health access to transferring resources to states, reducing clarity about intended outcomes.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.5","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The assessment covers 2022 program design and is relevant to the 2023 administrative baseline.","ruler_attribution":"The priority programs were part of the federal administration’s social-policy architecture.","limitations":["The report evaluates program design and monitoring, not the president’s personal decisions or 2023 service outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c27c10e952de9faf","start_unit":38,"end_unit":40,"fact_summary":"Program coverage in 2021 varied sharply: pensions and major education scholarships exceeded 70% coverage, while Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro, Universidades para el Bienestar and emergency assistance were below 17%. Some apparent improvements resulted from redefining the target population; for example, disability-pension coverage rose from 14% to 65% largely because the target population fell by 74%.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.10","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The findings concern 2021 results, reported in 2022, and provide context for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The programs were administered under López Obrador’s government.","limitations":["Coverage changes may reflect measurement and target-population revisions rather than actual equivalent welfare gains."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c27c10e952de9faf","start_unit":42,"end_unit":51,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL found that 56% of priority programs had adequate or outstanding target compliance in 2021, but the health program with the second-largest budget had deficient compliance, while the largest-budget adult-pension program was outstanding. Several programs deteriorated from 2020, and budget allocation showed almost no relationship to effective target compliance. The report identified weak target-setting, unclear populations and inconsistent sustained performance as continuing challenges.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","6B.5","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report evaluates 2021 results and 2022 budgets, serving as evidence about implementation capacity entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The programs and budget choices belonged to the federal administration under López Obrador.","limitations":["The report does not establish why budget allocations were made or whether later corrective action occurred."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus contains no direct evidence about nuclear weapons, proliferation controls, arms control, AI or other existential-risk safeguards specific to Mexico in 2023; those lenses are therefore not represented by facts.","Several sources report national or institutional outcomes and cannot establish López Obrador’s personal knowledge, intent or responsibility for every underlying event.","Some documents predate 2023 or provide 2022 baselines; period fit is stated for each fact."]}
